clinician.request: What were the results of the conjunctival secretions bacteriology?
clinician.current_trajectory_hypothesis: Patient presented with purulent conjunctivitis and peri-orbital edema after dog contact, while immunocompromised due to chemotherapy. Initial workup included conjunctival cultures. The hypothesis is that these cultures will identify Pasteurella multocida.
missing_key_evidence: Identification of causative organism from conjunctival cultures

report.source_text: Conjunctival secretions were sampled on admission for bacteriological analysis and cultured on blood agar. Direct examination showed numerous leukocytes and rare gram-negative bacilli (Figure 1C). Regular, grey, smooth colonies grew the next day. The oxidase test was positive for the 1-3 mm diameter, non-hemolytic colonies (Figure 1D&E), strongly suggesting that the isolated strain belonged to Pasteurella genus. The involvement of Pasteurella multocida was also strongly suggested here by mannitol fermentation (API-20E Array) (Figure 1F) and confirmed by MALDI TOF mass spectrometry.

Conjunctival cultures identified Pasteurella multocida. The initial CT scan showed no intra-orbital extension, suggesting pre-septal cellulitis, but explicit confirmation is needed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old immunocompromised male presented with purulent conjunctivitis, peri-orbital edema, and fever after dog contact. Clinical examination revealed inflammatory edema of the eyelids, skin rupture, and purulent encystment. A CT scan showed no intra-orbital extension, consistent with pre-septal cellulitis. Conjunctival secretions cultured on admission identified Pasteurella multocida, confirmed by MALDI TOF mass spectrometry.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with purulent conjunctivitis, peri-orbital edema, and fever after dog contact.
Patient is immunocompromised due to chemotherapy for angioimmunoblastic-T-cell-lymphoma.
Clinical examination revealed inflammatory edema of both upper and lower lids, skin rupture and purulent encystment above and below his eye, consistent with pre-septal cellulitis.
CT scan showed no evidence of intra-orbital extension, supporting a diagnosis of pre-septal cellulitis.
Conjunctival secretions showed numerous leukocytes and gram-negative bacilli on direct examination.
Culture of conjunctival secretions grew Pasteurella genus, and Pasteurella multocida was confirmed by MALDI TOF mass spectrometry.
